elements.evidence: "Vendor owns its generic tools and know-how."

elements.element: Customer licence to deliverables is perpetual
elements.evidence: "Customer's licence to each Deliverable is perpetual"
"The revocable, non-transferable, and Order Form term limitations ... do not apply"; "irrevocable"
"Customer may use, modify, and sublicense each Deliverable"

elements.element: Customer owns deliverables/work product with Vendor assignment
elements.evidence: "Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer." remains unchanged

elements.element: Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to embedded Vendor IP
elements.evidence: 14.3 "Vendor retains Vendor Technology ... the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies"

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: No Customer Data ownership language in this clause; definition notes "Vendor Technology does not include Customer Data"
No joint-ownership language; ownership allocated exclusively to Vendor/Customer respectively

reasons: The inserted 14.2A completes every atomic element of the fallback licence: perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and use/modify/sublicense for Customer's business, while confirming Vendor ownership of generic tools and know-how.

The insertion is minimal: it disapplies only the three identified limitations in Section 14.2 (revocable, non-transferable, Order Form term) rather than rewriting the clause, and adds no new exceptions or boilerplate.
Preferred is not met because Vendor ownership of Deliverables and assignment to Customer is untouched, which is consistent with the locked fallback target.
Intent preserved: Sections 14.2 and 14.3 remain effective, Vendor Technology retention and identification duties are unaffected, and no undefined terms or dangling mechanics are introduced.
